title: What does Joint Commission require for staff competency?
description: What Joint Commission's public materials say about staff competency, waived testing competence and the 2026 Accreditation 360 changes, as at November 2026.
shortAnswer: Joint Commission, the US accrediting organization for hospitals and other health care organizations, expects accredited organizations to provide education and training and to evaluate staff competence. Its public materials show that, since January 1, 2026, hospital requirements above the CMS Conditions of Participation sit in 14 National Performance Goals, one of which covers staff competence. For waived testing, competence must be assessed at orientation and at least annually using more than one method.
keyTakeaways: Joint Commission's full standards and elements of performance are licensed through its E-dition platform, so this page relies only on what Joint Commission publishes openly.

Accreditation 360, announced in June 2025, removed more than 700 hospital requirements and moved Joint Commission's own requirements into a National Performance Goals chapter effective January 1, 2026.

National Performance Goal 12, Health Professional Resource Management, includes provision of education and training and evaluation of staff competence, alongside verification that staff meet employment requirements and practice within scope.
The waived testing goal requires documented training for each test a person is authorized to perform and competence assessment at orientation and annually, using more than one method.
Joint Commission states Accreditation 360 does not introduce new expectations, so organizations compliant before 2026 are expected to remain compliant.
jurisdiction: United States (private national accreditation, used by many hospitals alongside CMS Conditions of Participation)
regulator: Joint Commission (independent accrediting organization); Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) sets the underlying Conditions of Participation
appliesTo: Hospitals and critical access hospitals accredited by Joint Commission, including those using accreditation for deemed status purposes
Other Joint Commission accreditation programs with Human Resources chapters, such as ambulatory, home care, laboratory, nursing care center and behavioral health care
Health care staffing firms certified under Joint Commission's Health Care Staffing Services program

sections.heading: What does Joint Commission publish about staff competency, and what is not public?

blocks.text: Joint Commission publishes summaries of its hospital National Performance Goals, a searchable library of standards FAQs, and program overviews, but the detailed standards and elements of performance are licensed. Its [standards page](https://www.jointcommission.org/en-us/standards) says the standards are available through the E-dition platform, which is complimentary for accredited organizations, with a 90-day free trial for organizations not yet accredited. Joint Commission also says a public version of the standards is available for its accreditation and certification programs.

This page is limited to what those public materials say as at November 2026. It does not quote or reconstruct paywalled elements of performance, standard numbers or survey scoring. Accredited organizations should confirm the exact requirements for their program in E-dition and in the Survey Process Guide, which Joint Commission says replaced the Survey Activity Guide and aligns with the Medicare State Operations Manual.

sections.heading: How did Accreditation 360 change hospital standards in 2026?

blocks.text: Accreditation 360 reorganized the hospital and critical access hospital manuals so that requirements based on the CMS Conditions of Participation are identified separately from Joint Commission's own requirements. According to the [Accreditation 360 overview](https://www.jointcommission.org/accreditation/accreditation-360), Joint Commission removed more than 700 requirements from the hospital accreditation program, building on a reduction of 400 announced in 2023.

Joint Commission's remaining requirements that go beyond the Conditions of Participation, together with the former National Patient Safety Goals, were merged into 14 National Performance Goals (NPGs). The NPG chapter became effective on January 1, 2026, replacing the National Patient Safety Goals chapter for hospitals. The 14 goals are Right Patient, Right Care; Culture of Safety; Emergency Management; Excellent Health Outcomes for All; Infection Prevention and Control; Pain Management; Patient Rights; Suicide Risk Reduction; Safe Transplant Practices; Waived (Point-of-Care) Testing; Workplace and Patient Safety; Planning and Evaluating Provision of Care; Imaging Safety; and Medication Management.

blocks.title: Joint Commission, Accreditation 360 FAQs
blocks.text: "Accreditation 360 does not introduce any new expectations. Organizations should continue to focus on complying with all current expectations. If an organization is currently compliant, it is expected that it will remain compliant under the Accreditation 360 revisions."

The changes described here are for hospitals and critical access hospitals. Joint Commission's FAQs treat the timing for non-acute programs as a separate question, so ambulatory, home care and other programs should check their own manuals. The standards FAQ library still lists a Human Resources (HR) chapter for hospital, critical access hospital, ambulatory, home care, laboratory, nursing care center and assisted living manuals.

sections.heading: What does National Performance Goal 12 say about staff competence?

blocks.text: The goal published as [National Performance Goal 12, Health Professional Resource Management](https://www.jointcommission.org/standards/national-performance-goals/health-professional-resource-management), lists the provision of education and training and the evaluation of staff competence among its requirements. Joint Commission says it elevated its planning for provision of care standards to a National Performance Goal in July 2025, and that these standards supplement the CMS Conditions of Participation for staffing with additional expectations for verification, training, education and ongoing performance improvement monitoring.

items: The leadership team ensures there is adequate qualified staff to meet the needs of the population served and determines how staff function within the organization.
The nurse executive directs implementation of nurse staffing plans.
The organization verifies that staff complete all requirements for employment and practice within their scope of practice.
The organization provides education and training and evaluates staff competence.
Staffing is evaluated during performance improvement activities, including as a factor when undesirable trends or variations exist.
Leadership evaluates its care delivery models, including newer models such as virtual nursing.

blocks.text: The public summary does not give an assessment interval or a required method for general clinical competence. Those details, where they exist, are in the licensed standards. For designing assessments that would stand up to any reviewer, see [how to design competency assessments](/guides/how-to-design-competency-assessments).

sections.heading: What competency does Joint Commission require for waived testing?

blocks.text: Waived testing is the clearest example of Joint Commission going beyond federal law. The CLIA regulations do not require competency assessment for staff in waived-only laboratories, but the hospital [waived testing National Performance Goal](https://www.jointcommission.org/standards/national-performance-goals/waived-testing) does. It requires that staff who perform waived testing have been trained for each test they are authorized to perform, with the training documented.

blocks.title: Joint Commission, National Performance Goal 10: Waived Testing
blocks.text: "Competence for waived testing is assessed and documented according to hospital policy at defined intervals, but at least at the time of orientation and annually thereafter. Competency is assessed using more than one method (e.g., performance of a test on a blind specimen, periodic observation of routine work, monitoring of quality control performance, written testing)."

Blood glucose, fecal occult blood and rapid strep tests are the examples Joint Commission gives, so the goal touches many nurses and other clinical staff, not only laboratory personnel. The standards FAQ library also has an entry, updated April 22, 2026, on whether licensed practitioners performing waived testing need competency assessment. For nonwaived testing, the CLIA six-procedure requirement applies; see [CLIA personnel competency assessment](/regulations/clia-laboratory-personnel-competency-requirements).

sections.heading: How does Joint Commission separate competency assessment from orientation and training?

blocks.text: Joint Commission treats orientation, education and training, and competency assessment as distinct activities. Its standards FAQ library includes entries titled Competency Assessment vs Orientation (updated April 21, 2026) and Competency Assessment vs Education and Training (updated June 24, 2026), which apply across the hospital, critical access hospital, ambulatory, home care, laboratory, nursing care center and assisted living manuals. The first describes the HR chapter as including requirements for both "orientation" and "competency assessment".

One published answer, written for the Health Care Staffing Services certification program, describes acceptable methods. It lists information from current and previous employers, peer feedback, verification of certification and licensure, written or oral tests, and observation of skills, and says the assessment must focus on the competency needs of the clinical staff member's assignment.

blocks.title: Joint Commission standards FAQ: Competency Assessment, Requirements
blocks.text: "Use of a self-assessment, such as a skills checklist, as the sole assessment method does not constitute a competency assessment."

That principle lines up with the waived testing goal's insistence on more than one method, and with the definition of [competency assessment](/glossary/competency-assessment) as a check against a stated standard rather than a record of attendance or a self-rating.

sections.heading: How can a hospital map these expectations to roles and evidence?

blocks.text: Organize by the expectation, the roles it touches, the interval stated in a public source, and the evidence a surveyor is likely to ask for. Where the public material gives no interval, the table says so, and the hospital's own policy must fill the gap.

blocks.text: Because Joint Commission's hospital standards build on the CMS Conditions of Participation, a hospital's register should include the federal training duties too; see [CMS hospital Conditions of Participation training](/regulations/cms-hospital-conditions-of-participation-training) and, for laboratories, the [CMS competency brochure](https://www.cms.gov/regulations-and-guidance/legislation/clia/downloads/clia_compbrochure_508.pdf). A [training matrix](/guides/how-to-build-a-training-matrix) can hold both sets of obligations against the same roles.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry records each accreditation expectation and each federal requirement as separate obligations linked to the same roles and competencies, so a hospital can see where accreditation adds to the federal floor, as with waived testing. Assessment methods are attached to each competency, which makes a reliance on self-assessment alone visible. See how this works for [healthcare and life sciences organizations](/industries/healthcare-life-sciences).

faqs.q: Are Joint Commission standards free to read?
faqs.a: Partly. Joint Commission publishes National Performance Goal summaries, standards FAQs and program information openly, and says a public version of the standards is available. The full manuals are provided through the E-dition platform, complimentary for accredited organizations, with a 90-day free trial for organizations that are not yet accredited.

Joint Commission says Accreditation 360 does not introduce new expectations and that organizations compliant before the change are expected to remain compliant. Its public National Performance Goal 12 summary still lists provision of education and training and evaluation of staff competence, and the waived testing goal keeps orientation and annual competence assessment.

faqs.q: Does Joint Commission require annual competency assessment for all staff?
faqs.a: The public materials reviewed for this page state an annual minimum only for waived testing. For other clinical competence, the public NPG 12 summary does not give an interval. Hospitals should check the licensed standards for their program and set the interval in their own competency policy.

faqs.q: Is a skills checklist enough to show competence?
faqs.a: Not on its own if it is a self-assessment. A published Joint Commission standards FAQ states that a self-assessment, such as a skills checklist, used as the sole method does not constitute a competency assessment. Combining it with observation, testing or verified records gives an independent measure.

factCheck.claim: Accreditation 360 overview: removing more than 700 requirements from the hospital accreditation program, building on 400 removed in 2023; manual identifies CMS CoPs and JC NPGs; public version of standards available.

A360 FAQs: announced June 2025; CoP-based requirements differentiated, remaining JC requirements and NPSGs merged into NPGs; 14 NPGs listed by name; A360 does not introduce new expectations (quoted); survey process unchanged; Survey Process Guide replaces Survey Activity Guide and aligns with State Operations Manual; separate FAQ entry on timing for non-acute programs (answer not relied on).
Standards page: NPG chapter effective January 1, 2026, replacing NPSG chapter; E-dition complimentary for accredited organizations; 90-day free trial; public standards available.

NPG 12 page: elevated to NPG in July 2025; standards supplement CMS CoPs for staffing with verification, training, education and PI monitoring; requirements include verification of employment requirements and scope, provision of education and training and evaluation of staff competence, nurse executive staffing plans, care delivery model evaluation.

NPG 10 waived testing: staff trained for each test with training documented; competence assessed and documented at orientation and annually, using more than one method (quoted with examples); examples of waived tests: blood glucose, fecal occult blood, rapid strep.

Standards FAQ (HSHR, first published Apr 11, 2016, updated Feb 8, 2022): competency assessment methods; self-assessment such as a skills checklist as sole method does not constitute competency assessment.

Standards FAQ search results for "competency" list Competency Assessment vs Orientation (updated April 21, 2026; HR chapter includes orientation and competency assessment), Competency Assessment vs Education and Training (updated June 24, 2026), and Licensed Practitioners Waived Testing Competency (updated April 22, 2026), with manuals listed.
CMS: CLIA does not require competency assessment for testing personnel in waived-only laboratories.
